name: mkvalidator
desc: Tool to verify Matroska and WebM files for spec conformance
why: Checks Matroska and WebM files against the spec, a way into the structure of container formats, though a narrow one.

brief.what_it_is: mkvalidator is a command line tool that checks Matroska and WebM files for spec conformance. It reads a file and looks for bogus or missing key elements, comparing them against the EBML DocType version declared in the file. It reports errors and warnings to the terminal. The page does not describe its output format beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The page describes it as a simple command line tool to verify Matroska and WebM files for spec conformance. It is published by the Matroska project itself, alongside the mkclean and libraries downloads.
brief.how_it_works: It checks the various bogus or missing key elements against the EBML DocType version of the file. It is built on libmatroska2 and libebml2, with Core-C providing an object API on top of C. The page does not describe the validation pipeline in more detail.
brief.install_notes: The page offers a source package and a pre-built binary for win64. It depends on libebml2 and libmatroska2 (both BSD-3-Clause), which in turn rely on Core-C. The libmatroska2 build enables minilzo support by default. The page gives no build steps, no macOS or Linux instructions, and no runtime configuration.
brief.standout: It validates against the EBML DocType version declared inside each file rather than a single fixed rule set. It is an official reference-style checker from the Matroska project, which gives a direct way to see how the spec is applied to real files.
brief.status: quiet. The page says the latest release is v0.6.0 from 2021-01-31. I could not see a last commit date from the homepage, so recent development activity is unknown.
brief.caveats: The minilzo support in libmatroska2 is GPL-2.0-or-later and is on by default, which changes the license of the resulting binary to GPL-2.0-or-later. The only pre-built binary mentioned is for win64. The page gives no usage examples, no sample output, and no list of which checks it performs. The homepage was reachable, but I did not follow the ChangeLog or source links.
quotes: mkvalidator is a simple command line tool to verify Matroska and WebM files for spec conformance.
It checks the various bogus or missing key elements against the EBML DocType version of the file and reports the errors/warnings in the command line.
